title: K-Concatenation Maximum Sum
statement: Form a longer array by placing `k` copies of the integer array `arr` one after another. Return the largest total of any contiguous stretch of this longer array. A stretch may be empty, in which case its total is 0, so the answer is never negative. Because the answer can be huge, return it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

Building all `k` copies and running Kadane's algorithm would touch up to 10^10 values. But the best stretch has only a few shapes: it lies inside one copy, or it starts in one copy and ends in a later one. Two copies back to back already contain every such shape with no whole copies in the middle. Each whole copy added in the middle changes the total by `total` (the sum of `arr`), so extra copies help exactly when `total > 0`, and then we want all `k - 2` of them.

## Approach

1. Run Kadane's algorithm over `min(k, 2)` copies: `current` is the best total of a stretch ending at the current value (empty allowed, so never below 0), and `best` is the largest `current` seen.
2. Add up `arr` into `total`.
3. If `k > 2` and `total > 0`, the best two-copy stretch crosses the copy boundary, so widen it with the `k - 2` whole copies in between: `best += (k - 2) * total`.
4. Return `best % MOD`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [1, 2]`, `k = 3`. Over two copies `[1, 2, 1, 2]`, `current` becomes `1, 3, 4, 6`, so `best = 6`. Then `total = 3`, which is positive and `k = 3 > 2`, so `best = 6 + 1 * 3 = 9`. The answer is `9`, the whole repeated array.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): at most two passes of Kadane plus one pass for the sum.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- With `k = 1` only one copy exists; scanning two would overcount.
- Add the middle copies only when `total > 0`; with a zero or negative sum they never help.
- The true maximum can reach about 10^14: keep `best` in a 64-bit type (`long` in Java, `long long` in C) and take the modulo only at the end, since reducing earlier would break the comparisons.
- The empty stretch makes the answer at least 0, so an all-negative `arr` returns 0.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MOD` | the modulus 10^9 + 7 |
| `best` | largest stretch total found |
| `current` | best total of a stretch ending at the current value |
| `rounds`, `round` | how many copies Kadane scans (1 or 2), and which one |
| `value` | the current element |
| `total` | sum of one copy of `arr` |

narration.3: The empty stretch is allowed, so the best total starts at 0.
narration.4: current is the best total of a stretch that ends at the value being read.
narration.5: Two copies hold every stretch shape without whole copies in the middle; with k = 1 there is only one copy.
narration.7: Scan the array once or twice, as if the copies were laid side by side.
narration.9: Either extend the stretch ending at the previous value, or restart with an empty one if the sum went negative.
narration.10: Remember the largest stretch total seen so far.
narration.15: Add up one copy of arr...
narration.16: ...to get total, what each extra whole copy contributes.
narration.18: Extra copies only help when there are more than two and each one adds a positive amount.
narration.19: Widen the best boundary-crossing stretch with the k - 2 whole copies in between.
narration.21: Reduce the answer modulo 10^9 + 7 only at the very end.
